name: Override
headline: Your windows. Your way.
summary: A macOS menu bar app for configurable window management. Choose how windows hide, minimize, fill your display, and snap into place. Available as a beta.
compatibility: For Apple silicon Macs running macOS 27 or later.

features.title: Choose what your window controls do.
paragraphs: Optionally make the close button request that an app quit, make minimize stash a window, or make zoom fill the usable display without entering macOS full screen. The app still controls its own save prompts and whether it quits.
Configure hide and minimize behavior globally or give individual applications their own rules. A stashed window is minimized and remembered so you can restore it from Override.

features.title: Make room for the task at hand.
paragraphs: Snap windows into halves, thirds, quarters, or a fill-display layout from the menu bar. Enable drag-to-edge snapping, adjust the gap between windows, or create custom grid layouts.

Directional keyboard shortcuts move or grow the focused window. Supported snapped neighbours can resize together along a shared edge. Results depend on the window controls and size limits exposed by each app.

features.title: Keep native behaviour within reach.
paragraphs: Optional overrides start off. Grant Accessibility access, then enable only the behaviours you want. Pause all overrides from the menu bar or exclude particular applications.
Restore stashed windows and undo the last supported window action when its target is still available. Interception is best-effort; unsupported or unsafe targets can retain native macOS behaviour.
